- Tell me about a case where you quickly integrated into a new team.
- Tell me about a case where the team helped you achieve a better result.
- Tell me about a case where you helped the team achieve a result.
- Tell me about a case where you took on part of someone else’s work for the sake of the overall result.
- Tell me about a case where you supported a colleague who was stuck.
- Tell me about a case where a colleague supported you in a difficult situation.
- Tell me about a case where you had to take over a critical task from someone else.
- Tell me about a case where you had to quickly transfer context to a colleague.
- Tell me about a case where you worked in a distributed or remote team.
- Tell me about a case where you had to work with colleagues in a different time zone.
- Tell me about a case where you had to establish collaboration between frontend and backend.
- Tell me about a case where you had to establish collaboration between development, QA, design, and product.
- Tell me about a case where you coordinated the work of several people without formal authority.
- Tell me about a case where you acted as a bridge between multiple teams.
- Tell me about a case where you had to explain a complex technical solution to your team.
- Tell me about a case where you had to explain development constraints to non-technical colleagues.
- Tell me about a case where you achieved a result thanks to good communication, not just a technical solution.
- Tell me about a case where poor communication in the team led to a problem.
- What would you do differently in a situation where team collaboration broke down?
- What do you do to reduce the risk of misunderstanding in a team?
- How do you document decisions so the team does not lose context?
- How important is written communication to you?
- How do you write messages in a way that is useful to the team?
- How do you conduct discussion in chat without creating chaos?
- How do you document technical decisions so others can easily understand them?
- How do you do a handoff for a task or project?
- How do you transfer knowledge within a team?
- How do you feel about pair programming?
- When is pair programming useful, and when is it not?
- Have you used mob programming or ensemble programming? What was the result?
- How do you view code review as a teamwork tool?
- What is a good code review to you?
- How do you respond to comments in a code review?
- How do you formulate comments in a code review so as not to demotivate a colleague?
- What should you do if you disagree with a comment in a code review?
- What should you do if two people on a team understand quality standards differently?
- How do you help establish shared engineering standards in a team?
- How do you feel about team agreements on code style, architecture, and processes?
- What do you do if you disagree with a team agreement?
- What do you do if the team is used to working chaotically, but you need a more structured approach?
- How do you act if you see that there is a bus factor in the team and knowledge is concentrated in one person?
- What do you do to make sure knowledge is not locked in individual people’s heads?
- How do you help onboard new people into the team?
- Have you ever written onboarding documentation or run introductory sessions?
- How do you determine that a new person has adapted successfully to the team?
- What do you do if there is a quiet strong specialist on the team whom no one hears?
- What do you do if there is a very active person on the team who suppresses others?
- How do you behave in meetings to make discussion productive?
- How do you determine that a meeting is unnecessary and the issue is better solved asynchronously?
- How do you prepare for team meetings?
- How do you capture the outcomes of meetings?
- How do you make sure agreements reached after meetings are followed through?
- What do you do if the team keeps going in circles in meetings and cannot make a decision?
- How do you act if part of the team comes to a discussion unprepared?
- How do you act if the discussion goes too deep into details and loses sight of the goal?
- How do you act if one person monopolizes the discussion?
- How do you act if the team avoids difficult conversations?
- How do you behave if you see that the team’s decision is hurting quality, but everyone wants to “just move on”?
- How do you express disagreement in a team constructively?
- How do you maintain trust in a team?
- What, in your opinion, destroys trust in a team most strongly?
- How do you rebuild trust if you have let the team down?
- What do you do if a colleague lets the team down?
- How do you react if someone takes credit for your contribution?
- How do you react if your contribution is undervalued?

- Tell me about a case where you proposed an idea that no one supported at first.

### 2.11 Ethics, Responsibility, Security, and Quality
- What does professional responsibility as an engineer mean to you?
- Where does “I was just doing the task” end and the developer’s personal responsibility begin?

- What does “doing work with quality” mean to you?
- How do you determine that a solution is of sufficient quality for release?
- When is it acceptable to release a solution with known limitations?
- When is it no longer acceptable to release a solution with known issues?
- What do you do if you realize a task cannot be done well within the given deadline?
- How do you act if a manager asks you to “cut corners” to meet a deadline?
- How do you act if you realize that a solution is unsafe but the business wants to release as soon as possible?
- What do you do if you notice a potential vulnerability in the product?
- What would you do if you discovered that users’ personal data was ending up in logs?
- What would you do if you accidentally got access to data you should not have been able to see?
- What do you do if a critical vulnerability is discovered in production right before an important launch?
- What is more important: quickly closing the hole or first gathering full information? What does it depend on?
- How do you act if you see a colleague ignoring security issues?
- How do you act if a colleague regularly pushes low-quality code into critical parts of the system?
- How do you act if you see that the team systematically sacrifices quality for speed?
- How do you know that technical debt has already become a business risk?
- When is it worth insisting on improving quality even if it is unpopular?
- How do you convince stakeholders to invest in quality and reliability?
- How do you explain that “it works now” does not always mean “it is fine for production”?
- What do you do if you discover a problem that you were not formally responsible for noticing, but you have already noticed it?
- What do you do if an error is not in your area of responsibility, but you understand that it may be costly?
- Should a developer take responsibility for problems after release?
- How should responsibility be distributed between a developer, reviewer, tester, manager, and business?
- How do you feel about blame culture vs a culture of learning?
- How do you draw the line between responsibility and looking for someone to blame?
- How do you react if your code caused a production incident?
- What is the first thing you do if you realize the problem is caused by your change?
- How do you tell the team about your mistake?
- How do you act if users or the business were affected because of your mistake?
- After an incident, what is more important: fixing it quickly or deeply understanding the cause? How do you balance that?
- How do you participate in a postmortem after your own mistake?
- How would you describe a good postmortem?
- What should never be done in a postmortem?
- How do you make sure that errors in a team lead to improving the system rather than just causing stress?
- What do you do if leadership starts looking for someone to blame instead of looking for causes during an incident?
- How do you know when a bug is random and when it is a sign of a systemic problem?
- What do you consider an unacceptable compromise in quality?
- What do you consider an unacceptable compromise in security?
- Are there situations where you would refuse to do a task? Which ones?
- What would you do if you were asked to implement functionality that could harm users?
- What would you do if the requirements are legal but seem ethically questionable to you?
- Should an engineer argue with the business for ethical reasons? When?
- Under what conditions are you ready to escalate a problem higher up the chain?
- What would you do if management asked you to hide a problem from a client or user?
- What would you do if you were asked to downplay the severity of an incident in a report?
- What would you do if you saw that metrics or reports were being interpreted dishonestly or manipulatively?
- What would you do if you were asked to collect more user data than is actually needed?
- How do you understand the principle of data minimization?
- Why is it important for a developer to think about privacy even if the company has lawyers and a security team?
- What do you do if you see that the product does not have sufficient restrictions on access to data?
- How do you feel about the principle of least privilege?
- What do you do if permissions in the company are granted too broadly?
- How do you feel about “temporary exceptions” in security that constantly become permanent?
- What do you consider good engineering hygiene in security matters?
- How do you feel about copying production data into test environments?
- In what cases is using real user data in development unacceptable?
- What do you think about logging full requests and responses?
- When does observability begin to conflict with privacy and security?
- How do you balance developer convenience with system security?
- When is it acceptable to “grant access right now and sort it out later”? Is it acceptable at all?
- What do you think about storing secrets in code, .env files, CI, or secret stores?
- How do you react if you see a token or password in a repository?
- What do you do if you find a vulnerability in another service inside the company?
- What do you do if you see that an external dependency in the project is vulnerable?
- How do you decide whether to urgently update the dependency or postpone it?
- What do you do if updating dependencies breaks part of the system but closes a serious risk?
- How do you explain to the team and management the value of regular security and quality practices?
- How do you know that a team is mature in matters of quality?
- How do you know that a team is mature in matters of security?
- Which engineering practices have the strongest impact on product quality?
- Which engineering practices have the strongest impact on product security?
- How do you feel about mandatory pre-release checklists?
- Which checks do you consider mandatory before release?
- What would you include in a quality gate for a production release?
- What would you include in a security gate for a production release?
- How do you feel about the formula “move fast and break things”?
- Where is the line between pragmatism and negligence?
- What do you do if you do not have enough time, people, or context to guarantee quality?
- How do you act if you do not have full confidence in the correctness of a solution, but a decision must be made now?
- How do you communicate risks in a way that they will be heard?
- How do you document accepted compromises and conscious risks?
- Who should decide whether a risk is acceptable: the engineer, team lead, manager, or business? Why?
- Can a feature be released if you are not sure it will not worsen the user experience?
- What is more important: the perfect solution or transparent understanding of the risks? Why?

- How do you determine the priority of fixing a defect?
- How do you determine which incidents need to be escalated immediately?
- Have you ever stopped a release? Why, and how did you justify it?
- Have you ever argued for quality when others wanted to “ship as is”?
- Have you ever had to admit that you underestimated a risk? What did you do afterward?

### 13.14 Architecture interviews: defending decisions and trade-offs
- How do you usually start an architecture interview or a system design section?
- What clarifying questions do you ask before proposing an architecture?
- What product requirements do you want to understand first?
- What non-functional requirements do you clarify before starting the design?
- What assumptions do you state out loud if the requirements are incomplete?
- How do you define the scope of the problem if the interviewer states it too broadly?
- How do you decide what is truly important in the problem and what can be deferred?
- How do you estimate rough load if no concrete numbers are given?
- What questions about traffic, growth, latency, and SLA would you ask at the beginning?
- What questions about security, privacy, and compliance would you ask at the beginning?
- What questions about data, consistency, and retention would you ask at the beginning?
- What questions about product scenarios and UX would you ask before designing the system?
- Why is it dangerous to start system design immediately with microservices, cache, and Kafka?
- Why is it important in an architecture interview to first describe a high-level design rather than diving into details?
- How do you explain to the interviewer why you start with a simple solution?
- Why does “the most complex architecture” not mean “the best solution”?
- How do you distinguish good engineering complexity from excessive complexity?
- How do you know that a project needs a monolith rather than microservices?
- How do you defend choosing a monolith if the interviewer is clearly expecting microservices?
- How do you defend choosing a modular monolith as an intermediate solution?
- How do you justify that the architecture should not be made more complex yet?
- How do you explain why you propose this specific set of components?
- Why did you choose SQL rather than NoSQL?
- Why did you choose NoSQL rather than SQL?
- Why did you choose PostgreSQL rather than MySQL?
- Why did you choose Elasticsearch/OpenSearch rather than a database for search?
- Why did you choose Redis rather than simply hitting the database more often?
- Why did you choose Kafka rather than RabbitMQ?
- Why did you choose RabbitMQ rather than Kafka?
- Why did you choose synchronous communication rather than messaging?
- Why did you choose messaging rather than direct REST/gRPC calls?
- Why did you choose GraphQL rather than REST?
- Why did you choose REST rather than GraphQL?
- Why did you choose gRPC rather than HTTP/JSON?
- Why did you choose WebSocket rather than polling?
- Why did you choose SSE rather than WebSocket?
- Why did you choose eventual consistency rather than strong consistency?
- Why did you choose strong consistency even though it is more expensive in terms of latency and availability?
- What trade-offs do you most often articulate in a system design answer?
- What trade-offs between latency, throughput, and cost do you consider?
- What trade-offs between simplicity and extensibility do you consider?
- What trade-offs between time-to-market and architectural purity do you consider acceptable?
- What trade-offs between reliability and development speed do you consider reasonable?
- What trade-offs between developer experience and operational complexity do you consider?
- How do you explain why the solution fits the current stage of the product?
- How do you explain how the architecture will evolve over time?
- How do you show that you are thinking not only about launch but also about supporting the solution?
- How do you justify service or module boundaries?
- How do you determine where the bounded context lies in a problem?
- How do you know that two components should be separate services rather than modules?
- Why is decomposition by technical layers often worse than decomposition by domains?

- How do you justify the choice of primary keys, indexes, and storage strategy?
- How do you defend the caching strategy?

- How do you defend the cache invalidation strategy?
- How do you explain the risks of cache stampede and stale data?
- How do you justify the need for a queue?
- How do you defend the decision to use a broker if cron jobs and a database would suffice?

- How do you defend your approach to data consistency across services?
- Why did you choose saga rather than a distributed transaction?
- Why did you choose outbox rather than “update the database first, then send the event”?
- How do you explain idempotency in your design?
- How do you defend the retry approach?
- How do you justify having a DLQ?
- How do you explain the strategy for handling partial failures?
- How do you show that you have thought about dependency failures?
- How do you defend the chosen retry policy?

## 16. Leadership, Management, and Staff+ Level

### 16.1 Transition from IC to Leadership
- Why did you decide to move from individual contributor to leadership?
- What attracts you more in a leadership role than in an individual contributor role?
- Why do you want to be a lead rather than remain a strong senior/staff engineer?

- What expectations do you think are usually mistakenly associated with a leadership role?

- Which part of leadership work was the hardest for you?
- What turned out to be the most unpleasant or uncomfortable part of the transition from IC to leadership?

- What did you gain by moving from IC to leadership?
- What was emotionally the hardest part of this transition for you?
- How do you explain to yourself that your contribution is no longer always expressed in code?
- How do you assess your effectiveness as a leader if you write less code?
- How do you determine that you bring more value as a leader than as an individual contributor?
- Which is harder: solving a difficult technical problem yourself or organizing the work of others so that the problem is solved by the team?

- How did your attitude toward deadlines, quality, and trade-offs change after moving from IC?

## 18.3 Debugging Tasks
- You have a program that “sometimes works, sometimes doesn’t.” Where do you start debugging?
- Which steps do you usually go through when investigating a bug from the first report to the fix?
- How do you distinguish a code problem from a data, configuration, or environment problem?
- What would you do first if a bug reproduces only for the user, but not locally for you?
- How do you gather the minimum set of facts before starting debugging?
- What is a minimal reproducible example and how do you build one?
- How do you narrow down the search area if the codebase is large?
- How do you determine in which commit the defect appeared?
- How do you use `git bisect` to find a regression?
- How do you determine that a bug is actually a bug rather than an incorrect expectation of the system?
- What would you do if the bug report is very vague: “something is sometimes slow”?
- What questions would you ask the person who reported the bug?
- How do you document reproduction steps so another engineer can reproduce the issue?
- How do you determine whether a bug affects one user, a group of users, or the whole system?
- How do you prioritize bugs by severity?
- What is the difference between an incident, a defect, a regression, and a flaky issue?
- How do you search for a problem when only the symptom is known, but not the cause?
- Which artifacts do you analyze during debugging: logs, metrics, traces, dumps, profiles?
- When are logs enough, and when do you need metrics and tracing?
- How do you decide where to temporarily add extra logs for investigation?
- How do you avoid “breaking” the system behavior while debugging?
- Why is print-debugging sometimes useful and sometimes harmful?
- When should you use a debugger, and when is it better to analyze logs and traces?
- How do you use breakpoints effectively?
- What is a conditional breakpoint and when is it especially useful?
- How do you debug code that runs asynchronously?
- How do you debug multithreaded or concurrent code?
- Why can a race condition disappear when you add logs or breakpoints?
- How do you search for a problem that reproduces only under load?
- How do you search for a memory leak?
- How do you determine that the problem is related to a memory leak rather than simply a large volume of data?
- How do you search for a CPU bottleneck?
- How do you investigate a sudden increase in API response time?
- How do you investigate performance degradation after a release?
- What do you do if the service starts using too much memory after deployment?
- What do you do if the application starts crashing periodically without an obvious reason?
- How do you investigate an intermittent bug that appears rarely?
- How do you increase the likelihood of reproducing a rare bug?
- What do you do if a bug reproduces only in production?
- When is it acceptable to debug directly in production, and when is it dangerous?
- How do you safely collect additional diagnostics in production?
- How would you investigate a problem if after deployment some users started getting 500 errors?
- How do you determine whether the issue is related to a specific server, region, node, container, or application version?
- How do you check the hypothesis that the problem is caused by a feature flag or configuration?
- How do you search for a bug that appears only with certain data in the database?
- What do you do if a bug depends on a time zone, locale, or date format?
- How do you debug an issue related to DST, a time zone, or a midnight boundary?
- How do you find an off-by-one bug?
- How do you search for a rounding bug or a decimal/float issue?
- How do you check whether there is a bug caused by null/undefined/None/nil values?
- How do you search for a problem caused by incorrect initialization order?
- How do you debug an issue related to caching?
- How do you prove that stale cache is the source of the issue rather than the database?
- How do you search for a cache invalidation bug?
- How do you investigate a problem where “the data is in the DB, but not in the UI”?
- How do you determine which side the issue is on: frontend, backend, DB, network, CDN, proxy?
- How do you investigate a CORS issue if the request works from Postman but not in the browser?
- How do you search for bugs related to cookies, sessions, and authentication?
- How would you debug the problem “the user gets logged out periodically”?
- How do you search for an error in an OAuth/OIDC flow?
- How do you debug JWT issues: expiration, signature, clock skew?
- What would you check if users complain about duplicate actions after clicking a button?
- How do you search for double form submission or repeated message processing?
- How do you debug an idempotency issue?
- How do you investigate message loss in a queue?
- How do you search for the cause of repeated message delivery from a broker?
- How do you debug an order-dependent bug, where the issue depends on the sequence of events?
- How do you search for a problem in a distributed system if each service “looks fine” individually?
- Why is a correlation ID needed and how does it help in debugging?
- How do you use distributed tracing when investigating a bug?
- How do you determine exactly where the chain of calls between services breaks?
- How would you search for a timeout problem in an external integration?
- How do you distinguish between a timeout, a retry storm, and a cascading failure?
- What would you check if one service’s API suddenly started returning more errors to another service?
- How do you search for a problem in a reverse proxy or load balancer?
- How do you investigate a bug related to Nginx/Ingress if the application works locally?
- How do you search for a problem in DNS or service discovery?
- How do you determine that the bug is caused not by the application, but by the infrastructure?
- How do you investigate a rise in 429 responses?
- How do you debug a rate limiting problem?
- How would you search for a deadlock in an application or database?
- How do you identify database locks as the cause of degradation?
- How do you determine that the problem is related to connection pool exhaustion?
- How do you debug an N+1 problem if users complain about slow pages?
- How do you search for a problem in ORM-generated queries?
- How do you debug flaky tests?
- How do you determine whether a flaky test is related to test data, time, concurrency, or the environment?
- How do you investigate the problem “tests pass locally, but fail in CI”?
- How do you search for a bug that occurs only in a Docker container?
- How do you investigate a problem that occurs only in Kubernetes?
- How do you debug readiness/liveness probe issues?
- What would you check if the container keeps restarting?
- How do you search for a problem in environment variables and secrets?
- How do you debug an error caused by a mismatch in library versions?
- How would you search for a dependency conflict problem?
- How do you investigate a bug after upgrading a framework or runtime?
- How do you track regressions after seemingly harmless refactoring?
- How do you search for a bug related to a database schema change?
- What do you check if a migration completed successfully, but the application started behaving incorrectly afterward?
- How do you search for a backward compatibility issue between an old and a new service version?
- How do you debug serialization/deserialization issues?
- What do you check if one service sends JSON and another cannot process it?
- How do you search for bugs at the boundary between different languages, formats, and protocols?
- How do you debug a frontend bug if in the UI “nothing happens”?
- How do you search for a bug if a React/Vue component rerenders too often?
- How do you investigate a memory leak in the browser?
- How do you search for bugs in event handlers, debounce/throttle, or asynchronous requests on the frontend?
- How do you debug a race condition between multiple requests in the UI?
- How do you search for a hydration mismatch issue in an SSR application?
- How do you investigate a bug related to feature flags on the client side?
- How do you search for an error in form state management?
- How do you debug a problem if an E2E test fails intermittently, but the scenario works manually?
- How do you search for an issue with a locator, asynchronous UI, or a timing issue in E2E?
- How do you verify that the identified cause is truly the root cause and not a side symptom?
- How do you confirm a hypothesis about the cause of a bug?
- Why is it dangerous to fix a bug before understanding the root cause?
- How do you distinguish a workaround from a real fix?
- When is it acceptable to release a temporary workaround?
- What is better: a quick targeted fix or a deeper refactoring? What does it depend on?
- How do you assess the risk of a fix before deployment?
- Which tests should be added after fixing a bug?
- Why is it important to write a regression test after a fix?
- What should you do if writing a regression test is difficult?
- How do you make sure the fix did not break other scenarios?
- How should you document a bug investigation and its resolution?
- What should be included in a postmortem after a complex incident?
- What conclusions would you draw after a bug that was hard to find for a long time?
- How would you explain the cause of a complex incident to a non-technical manager?
- How would you explain to the team the difference between a symptom, a trigger, and a root cause?
- Tell me about the most complex bug you investigated. How did you approach it?
- Tell me about a case when your first conclusion about the cause of a bug turned out to be wrong.
- Tell me about a case when the problem was caused not by the application, but by infrastructure or configuration.
- Tell me about a case when a bug was caused by a combination of several factors.
- Give an example of a bug that only appeared in production. How did you find it?
- Give an example of a bug where the problem was in the data, not in the code.
- Give an example of when you found the cause of a performance degradation.
- Give an example of when you resolved an incident under time pressure.
- Give an example of when you had to deeply understand someone else’s code to investigate an issue.
- Give an example of when fixing the symptom did not eliminate the root cause.
- What would you do if the bug is critical, but the root cause is still unclear?
- What would you do if a new, more serious problem appeared after the fix?
- How would you organize the debugging process in a team so that complex bugs are resolved faster?
- Which anti-patterns in debugging do you consider the most dangerous?
- Why is the phrase “I can’t reproduce it, so the bug doesn’t exist” harmful?
- Which is worse: too many logs or too few logs? Why?
- Which debugging tools do you consider must-have for a backend/frontend/fullstack engineer?
- How do you know when it is time to stop debugging manually and invest in observability, tests, and diagnostics?
- How would you teach a junior engineer to look for the root cause instead of just trying random fixes?

### 19.6 Checklists before an interview
- What do I know about the company, its product, market, and users?
- Do I understand exactly which role and level I am interviewing for?
- Can I clearly talk about myself in 1–2 minutes?
- Can I coherently talk about my experience in 2–3 minutes?
- What 3–5 strengths do I want to emphasize in this interview?
- What 1–2 weaknesses am I ready to discuss honestly and safely?
- Which 2–3 projects will I use as my main examples in the interview?
- Can I briefly describe each of these projects: goal, my role, stack, and result?
- Can I explain exactly what value I brought on each project?
- Can I name the most difficult technical problems I solved?
- Can I name my main mistakes and what they taught me?
- Can I explain why I am looking for a new job without negativity or complaints?
- Can I explain why I am interested in this specific company?
- Can I explain why I am interested in this specific role?
- Can I explain what matters to me in my next team and job?
- Have I prepared a clear story about my current job or latest project?
- Have I prepared a clear story about my favorite project?
- Have I prepared a clear story about a project I am proud of?
- Have I prepared a clear story about a failed project or a failed decision?
- Can I explain how I make technical decisions?
- Can I explain how I debug problems?
- Can I explain how I test my code?
- Can I explain how I work with requirements when they are incomplete or changing?
- Can I explain how I interact with designers, analysts, QA, DevOps, and managers?
- Can I explain how I work in a team and how I resolve conflicts?
- Can I explain how I learn and keep my skills up to date?
- Have I prepared answers to standard questions about motivation, expectations, and career goals?
- Have I prepared answers to questions about salary expectations?
- Have I prepared a strategy for answering uncomfortable questions about reasons for leaving, gaps, and failures?
- Do I know what I will say if I am asked to talk about myself without preparation?
- Do I know what I will say if I am asked to briefly describe my stack?
- Can I explain my stack in a way that is understandable both to a recruiter and to a technical interviewer?
- Can I quickly list the technologies I have actually worked with, without exaggerating?
- Do I know which technologies in my resume may trigger additional questions?
- Have I checked that I can honestly defend every line of my resume?
- Am I ready for the question: “What in your resume is most important for us?”
- Am I ready for the question: “Why do you have little commercial experience / no experience?”
- Am I ready for the question: “What makes you different from other candidates?”
- Am I ready for the question: “Why should we hire you specifically?”
- Have I prepared 5–10 STAR stories for different situations?
- Do I have a prepared story about a conflict in a team?
- Do I have a prepared story about a mistake and fixing its consequences?
- Do I have a prepared story about a missed deadline?
- Do I have a prepared story about taking initiative beyond my responsibilities?
- Do I have a prepared story about difficult feedback?
- Do I have a prepared story about helping a colleague?
- Do I have a prepared story about a situation where I did not know the answer and how I handled it?
- Do I have a prepared story about a situation where I chose a compromise?
- Do I have a prepared story about a situation where I disagreed with a team or manager decision?
- Do I have a prepared story about working under uncertainty?
- Have I prepared explanations for my main architectural or engineering choices?
- Have I prepared an explanation of why those particular technologies were used on the project?
- Have I prepared an explanation of the trade-offs in the chosen solution?
- Do I have examples where I improved performance, reliability, or DX?
- Do I have examples where I worked with legacy code?
- Do I have examples where I dealt with technical debt?
- Do I have examples where I wrote tests or improved quality?
- Do I have examples where I worked with production incidents?
- Do I have examples where I worked with monitoring, logs, or metrics?
- Do I have examples where I optimized database queries?
- Do I have examples where I worked with APIs, integrations, or external services?
- Do I have examples where I solved concurrency, asynchrony, or queue-related problems?
- Do I have examples where I dealt with security, access control, or data privacy?
- Do I have examples where I worked with CI/CD, releases, or infrastructure?
- Do I have examples where I improved UX, frontend performance, or accessibility?
- Do I have examples where I worked as a fullstack developer and aligned frontend and backend?
- Do I understand which algorithms and data structures questions are most likely for this role?
- Have I reviewed arrays, strings, hash tables, stack, queue, linked list, trees, and graphs?
- Have I reviewed Big O and can I explain the complexity of my solutions?
- Have I reviewed the basic problem-solving patterns: two pointers, sliding window, BFS/DFS, binary search, prefix sums, backtracking, heap, DP?
- Can I write code calmly and comment on my thought process?
- Do I understand how to explain brute force, optimization, and trade-offs?
- Am I ready to state assumptions out loud before I start coding?
- Am I ready to ask clarifying questions before solving a problem?
- Am I ready to first describe a simple solution and then improve it?
- Am I ready to test my solution against edge cases?
- Have I reviewed basic SQL queries?
- Have I reviewed JOIN, GROUP BY, HAVING, ORDER BY, LIMIT, subqueries, CTE, and window functions?
- Can I quickly explain the difference between INNER JOIN, LEFT JOIN, UNION, and UNION ALL?
- Can I explain indexes, transactions, isolation levels, and MVCC?
- Have I reviewed the basics of HTTP, REST, status codes, and idempotency?
- Have I reviewed the difference between authentication and authorization?
- Have I reviewed cookies, sessions, JWT, OAuth2, and OIDC?
- Have I reviewed the basic web vulnerabilities: XSS, CSRF, SQL injection, SSRF, IDOR?
- Have I reviewed networking basics: DNS, TCP, TLS, load balancer, reverse proxy?
- Have I reviewed the basics of Linux, Docker, CI/CD, logging, metrics, and tracing?
- Have I reviewed the key topics around caching, queues, and asynchrony?
- Have I reviewed the main differences between PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, and Redis?
- Have I reviewed the main frontend topics if I am interviewing for fullstack?
- Have I reviewed HTML, CSS, DOM, event loop, React, state management, rendering, and performance?
- Have I reviewed the main backend topics if I am interviewing for fullstack?
- Have I reviewed system design at a basic level if the role may touch it?
- Have I prepared 2–3 architecture problems and a template for approaching them?
- Can I start system design from requirements, load, and constraints?
- Can I discuss API, data, scaling, caching, reliability, observability, and security?
- Can I stay composed if I’m given a topic I haven’t designed in real life?
- Have I checked my resume for inconsistencies, exaggerations, and outdated wording?
- Have I reviewed my GitHub, pinned repositories, READMEs, demo links, and project descriptions?
- Have I reviewed my LinkedIn / Habr Career / hh profile if they are accessible to the interviewer?
- Have I checked that company names, dates, and roles match everywhere?
- Have I checked my setup before the online interview: camera, microphone, internet, battery?
- Have I checked my IDE, editor, terminal, language, and environment for live coding?
- Have I checked that I can share my screen without unnecessary tabs and notifications?
- Have I prepared a notebook or document for interview notes?
- Have I prepared water, a quiet place, lighting, and a neutral background?
- Have I prepared a backup communication channel in case the call has issues?
- Have I prepared my list of questions for the recruiter, manager, and team?
- Do I have questions about the product, process, culture, team, expectations, and growth?
- Do I have questions about the stack, quality, releases, on-call, incidents, and technical debt?
- Do I have questions about the success criteria for the first 3–6 months?
- Do I have questions about code review, testing, CI/CD, ownership, and decision-making?
- Do I have questions about the team, headcount, roles, and collaboration?
- Do I have questions about the roadmap, priorities, deadlines, and pressure?
- Do I have questions about the hiring process and the next steps?
- Have I thought through how to answer strange, projective, and inappropriate questions politely?
- Have I thought through where to set boundaries on personal and sensitive topics?
- Am I ready for a situation where I do not know the answer to a question?
- Am I ready to honestly say “I don’t know,” while still showing my reasoning?
- Am I ready for a situation where the interviewer interrupts or pressures me?
- Am I ready for a situation where the task seems not fully defined?
- Am I ready for a situation where the interviewer stays silent and expects me to lead the answer myself?
- Am I ready for a situation where the code does not compile or the solution does not come together right away?
- Am I ready for a situation where I’m given feedback during the interview itself?
- Am I ready for a situation where I’m asked to compare technologies I have limited hands-on experience with?
- Am I ready for a situation where I’m asked to defend a controversial decision from a past project?
- Am I ready for the question: “What would you do differently now?”
- Am I ready for the question: “What is your weakest area in the stack?”
- Am I ready for the question: “What will you do in your first 30/60/90 days?”
- Am I ready for the question: “What kind of offer are you looking for, and how will you choose?”
- Do I understand how to end an interview strongly: briefly, confidently, and to the point?
- Do I understand that I should not argue just for the sake of arguing, but I can disagree with clear reasoning?
- Do I understand that interviews evaluate not only knowledge, but also clarity of thought, communication, and maturity?
- Do I understand what my real competitive advantages are for this role?
- Do I understand the risks in my candidacy and how to address them proactively in my answers?
- Have I formulated for myself the main takeaway the interviewer should leave with after the meeting?
- What is the one main point I want the recruiter to remember about me?
- What is the one main point I want the technical interviewer to remember about me?
- What is the one main point I want the hiring manager to remember about me?
- If I’m asked to summarize, will I be able to do it briefly and confidently?
- If the interview goes worse than I hoped, do I know how to recover and not derail the rest of the conversation?
- If I have several interviews in a row, have I thought through how to maintain focus and energy?
- If I get an offer quickly, do I know which questions I need to clarify before accepting?
- If I get rejected, do I know how to extract maximum value from it and update my preparation checklist?

### 19.7 Reviewing Common Interview Questions and Traps
- What is the best way to answer the question “Tell me about yourself”?
- Why is it a bad answer to “Tell me about yourself” if the person starts retelling their resume from childhood onward?
- How do you avoid drifting into an answer that is too long for an open-ended question?
- What do interviewers want to hear in the question “Why are you interested in this role?”?
- What makes a good answer to “Why our company?” different from a generic one?
- How do you answer the question “Why are you looking for a new job?” safely and maturely?
- Why is it dangerous to speak too negatively about your current or past employer?
- How do you answer the question “Why did you leave your previous job?” without sounding defensive or conflict-oriented?
- How do you answer the question “What are your strengths?” without clichés?
- How do you answer the question “What are your weaknesses?” without shooting yourself in the foot?
- Why does the answer “I’m a perfectionist” usually not work?
- How do you answer the question “Why should we hire you?”?
- What are they really trying to assess with the question “Where do you see yourself in 3–5 years?”?
- How do you answer questions about salary expectations?
- What should you do if the recruiter pushes too early for a salary number?
- How do you react if you are asked about other offers or interview processes?
- How do you answer the question “Why don’t you have experience?” or “Why do you have little commercial experience?”?
- How do you sell pet projects if you have little commercial experience?
- What should you do if you are asked about a technology listed on your resume but only know it superficially?
- Why is it dangerous to exaggerate your level of proficiency with a technology?
- How do you answer honestly and advantageously to the question “Have you actually worked with this in production?”
- How do you properly answer the question “What exactly did you do personally, and what did the team do?”
- Why do interviewers like to clarify personal contribution rather than just the project’s overall success?
- How do you avoid taking sole credit for team achievements?
- How do you answer the question “What are you proud of?” without sounding pompous?
- How do you answer the question “Can you tell me about a mistake?” without retreating into a safe banality?
- What counts as a bad answer to a question about failure?
- How do you answer the question “Tell me about a conflict in the team”?
- Why is it dangerous to portray yourself as the only competent person while everyone else was incompetent?
- How do you answer the question “Tell me about difficult feedback you received”?
- How do you answer the question “Tell me about difficult feedback you gave to someone else”?
- How do you answer the question “Tell me about a time you missed a deadline”?
- How do you answer the question “Tell me about a time you made a decision with insufficient data”?
- What are they trying to assess with the question “Tell me about a time you disagreed with a manager / architect / colleague”?
- How do you show maturity in conflict rather than stubbornness?
- How do you answer the question “What will you do if you do not know the answer?”?
- What is better: staying silent, guessing, or honestly walking through your reasoning?
- How do you avoid getting lost on questions where you need to compare technologies?
- How do you answer the question “Why did you choose X over Y?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is the difference between A and B?” if you do not know the topic perfectly?
- What should you do if the question is phrased too broadly?
- What should you do if the question contains ambiguity or a hidden trap?
- Why is it useful to clarify the context of the question before answering?
- How do you avoid falling into the trap of “one correct answer” when in reality everything depends on trade-offs?
- What should you do if the interviewer intentionally simplifies the problem and is waiting to see whether you notice the nuances?
- What should you do if the interviewer asks about a technology you have not used but that you should still be able to compare conceptually?
- What should you do if you are asked to evaluate the “best” technology without context?
- Why are answers like “X is always better than Y” almost always dangerous?
- How do you answer the question “Monolith or microservices?”?
- How do you answer the question “PostgreSQL or MongoDB?”?
- How do you answer the question “REST or GraphQL?”?
- How do you answer the question “Java or Node.js?”?
- How do you answer the question “Redux or Zustand?”?
- How do you answer the question “Is Docker always necessary?”?
- How do you answer the question “Are tests always mandatory?”?
- How do you answer the question “Is it worth rewriting legacy?”?
- What should you do if the question feels artificial or detached from reality?
- How do you answer strange projective questions?
- What are they really evaluating with the question “What kind of animal do you see yourself as?”?
- How do you answer stress questions without irritation or sarcasm?
- How do you politely redirect the conversation if the question moves into an inappropriate personal area?
- What should you do if the interviewer asks an inappropriate or overly personal question?
- How do you answer a question that sounds like a test of loyalty rather than competence?
- How do you answer the question “Are you willing to work overtime?”?
- How do you answer the question “What matters more to you — life or work?”?
- How do you react to hidden red flags during the interview itself?
- How do you answer the question “Are you more of a team player or an individual contributor?”?
- How do you avoid being forced into a false dichotomy?
- What should you do if you are made to choose between speed and quality without context?
- How do you answer the question “What matters more: delivery or perfect code?”?
- How do you show a mature understanding of trade-offs in such questions?
- How do you answer the question “What is your favorite language / framework?” without sounding fanatical?
- Why is it dangerous to sound like a fan of a single technology?
- How do you answer the question “What do you dislike about your favorite language?”?
- How do you answer the question “What was the last book / article / technology you studied?”?
- What should you do if you have not read professional books recently but learn through practice and documentation?
- How do you answer the question “How do you keep up with new developments?” without listing random blogs?
- How do you answer the question “Why did you choose backend/frontend/fullstack?”?
- How do you answer the question “Why didn’t you go deeper into one specialization?” if you are fullstack?
- What should you do if the interviewer is skeptical about a fullstack positioning?
- How do you demonstrate depth in one axis and breadth across adjacent areas?
- How do you answer the question “What do you know about our company?” if information is limited?
- How do you answer the question “What is your most complex project?” if you have had only a few projects?
- How do you answer the question “What was the biggest high-load system you worked on?” if you have not worked on high load?
- How do you answer the question “What architectural decisions did you make?” if you were not an architect?
- How do you answer the question “What production incidents have you handled?” if you have little incident experience?
- How do you talk honestly about limited experience without diminishing yourself?
- What should you do if the interviewer asks senior-level questions while you are applying for a junior/middle role?
- How do you show potential if you do not yet have enough depth?
- How do you answer the question “What happens when a user enters a URL in the browser?”?
- Why is the question “What happens when a user enters a URL in a browser?” a trap question about the breadth of engineering fundamentals?
- How do you answer the question “What is JWT, and is it safe to use?”?
- Why is the question “What is JWT, and is it safe to use?” a trap question about understanding context rather than giving a textbook definition?
- How do you answer the question “What are microservices?” without reducing the answer to a buzzword?
- How do you answer the question “What is the event loop?” in a way that shows understanding rather than a memorized definition?
- How do you answer the question “What is caching, and where would you put it?” without sounding oversimplified?
- How do you answer the question “What is an index in a database?” without overcomplicating or oversimplifying it?
- How do you answer the question “How does a transaction work?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is the difference between a process and a thread?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is a race condition?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is the difference between authentication and authorization?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is idempotency?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is the difference between merge and rebase?”?
- How do you answer the question “What is the difference between unit and integration tests?”?
- How do you answer the question “When should you use SQL, and when should you use NoSQL?”?
- How do you answer the question “When should you use WebSocket versus polling / SSE?”?
- How do you answer the question “When do you need Docker, and when do you not?”?
- How do you answer the question “Why do you need CI/CD?” in a way that shows practical understanding?
- Why is it dangerous to answer too academically when they expect practical experience?
- Why is it dangerous to answer too pragmatically when they expect fundamental theory?
- How can you tell from the wording of a question whether they expect theory or practice?
- How do you answer a coding question if you do not see the optimal solution right away?
- What should you do if, during live coding, you can only come up with a brute-force solution at first?
- Why is it better to say a simple solution out loud first than to silently wait for the perfect one?
- How do you talk through edge cases during coding?
- How do you talk through test cases before running the code?
- How should you act if the interviewer stays silent and does not help during the coding exercise?
- What should you do if you did not finish writing the code in time?
- How do you wrap up a coding task if the solution is only partially complete?
- How do you answer a system design question if the problem is large and vague?
- Why is it important to start system design by clarifying requirements?
- What should you do if you do not immediately know which architecture to choose?
- How do you avoid drowning in details during system design?
- How do you avoid staying too abstract and high-level without enough specificity?
- What should you do if the interviewer suddenly changes the constraints in the middle of a design task?
- How do you react if the interviewer challenges the design you chose?
- How do you defend a solution without turning the conversation into an argument?
- Why is it important to acknowledge trade-offs rather than sell the solution as perfect?
- How do you answer the question “How would you design X?” if you have not actually built such a product before?
- What should you do if you do not remember the exact definition but understand the idea?
- When is it better to honestly say “I don’t remember the term, but I can explain the concept”?
- How do you answer a question with an obvious provocation or a clear “ego test”?
- How do you avoid downplaying your previous experience in an attempt to appear flexible?
- How do you avoid sounding overconfident without justification?
- How do you avoid sounding too uncertain if you only know the answer partially?
- How do you answer the question “What would you improve in our product?”?
- How do you answer the question “What would you do in your first few months in this role?”?
- How do you answer the question “How do you evaluate your own work?”?
- How do you answer the question “What does quality mean to you?”?
- How do you answer the question “What does ownership mean to you?”?
- How do you answer the question “What does it mean to be a senior / lead / professional?”?
- Why are questions about “value definitions” often more important than purely theoretical ones?
- How do you notice that the same question can be interpreted on several levels?
- How do you distinguish a knowledge question from a maturity question?
- How do you distinguish an experience question from a thinking question?
- How do you distinguish a communication question from a technical-depth question?
- What should you do if the interviewer asks the same question in different words?
- What should you do if it seems that the interviewer did not understand your answer?
- Should you proactively rephrase and structure your answer yourself?
- When is it useful to give a practical example, and when is it better to start with a general explanation?
- When is it useful to draw a diagram, table, or answer structure?
- How do you avoid going into too much detail if the interviewer is in a hurry?
- How do you avoid answering too briefly if the interviewer expects a more detailed answer?
- How do you calibrate the depth of your answer based on the interviewer’s reaction?
- What should you do if you feel your answer is going in the wrong direction?
- How do you gently correct yourself if you realize you made a mistake in your answer?
- Why is acknowledging a mistake while answering often a plus rather than a minus?
- What should you do if, after the interview, you realize you answered an important question poorly?
- What are common traps in recruiter interviews?
- What are common traps in technical interviews?
- What are common traps in system design interviews?
- What are common traps in managerial / leadership interviews?
- What are common traps in the HR stage?
- What are common traps in the final interview with the hiring manager?
- What are common traps in a “culture fit” interview?
- What are common traps in interviews for a first job?
- What are common traps in fullstack interviews?
- What are common traps in interviews when the candidate has little commercial experience but a lot of theory?
- What are common traps in interviews when the candidate has many pet projects but little team experience?
- What are common traps in interviews when the candidate tries to appear senior without a sufficient foundation?
- What are common traps in interviews when the candidate is too honest about all gaps without trying to compensate with good reasoning?
- How do you distinguish a difficult but normal question from a toxic interview?
- When should you continue the interview, and when should you mentally mark the company as a red flag?
- What should you do after an interview to turn every trap into a point for your next preparation?

## 20. Questions for the Company and the Interviewer

### 20.1 Questions for the Recruiter
- Can you briefly describe what this role is and why it is open?
- Is this a new position or a replacement for someone?
- Which team and product does this role belong to?
- What is the official internal title of the position?
- What work format is expected: office, hybrid, or remote?
- What time zone does the team work in?
- In which city or country is the employee hired?
- What type of employment is offered: employment contract, contractor status, freelance agreement, outsourcing?
- Is there a probation period? How long does it last, and how is successful completion evaluated?
- How is the hiring process usually structured at the company?
- How many interview stages should I expect?
- What exactly will the stages be: screening, technical interview, live coding, system design, final interview?
- Who will participate in the next stages?
- Is there a take-home assignment? If so, how much time is usually expected for it?
- Is there live coding? In which language or stack is it best to do it?
- Is there a stage focused on algorithms, system design, or architecture?
- Which topics should I pay special attention to when preparing?
- What is the core stack for this role?
- Which technologies are mandatory, and which are nice to have?
- What level are you looking for in this position?
- What are the main criteria you will use to evaluate the candidate?
- What would be a strong signal to you that a candidate is a good fit?
- What are the most common reasons candidates get rejected for this role?
- What is the company’s timeline for closing this vacancy?
- At what stage is the hiring process currently?
- How many candidates are currently being considered?
- How quickly do you usually provide feedback after each stage?
- In what format does the company provide feedback: general or more detailed?
- Is there an opportunity to receive more detailed feedback in case of rejection?
- What are the expectations regarding English proficiency for this role?
- How often is English actually used in the job?
- Are there international teams or overseas stakeholders?
- Does the company offer relocation or relocation support?
- Is work equipment provided: laptop, monitors, reimbursements?
- Is there reimbursement for internet, coworking, learning, or fitness?
- What benefits do employees receive?
- How are vacation, sick leave, and days off handled?
- Is there a flexible schedule?
- Are working hours fixed, or do results matter more?
- How financially stable is the company?
- How long has the company been around?
- How does the company make money?
- What stage is the company at: startup, growth, mature business, corporation?
- How would you describe the company culture in a few words?
- In your opinion, what do employees like most about working here?
- What challenges or specifics about working at the company are important to know in advance?
- What style of communication and collaboration is common in the company?
- How formalized are the processes?
- How does onboarding for new employees usually work?
- Is there an onboarding program for the first weeks or months?
- Is there a mentor during onboarding?
- How often do people leave this role or this team?
- What is the reason this vacancy is open specifically?
- What are the immediate tasks for the person in this role?
- What will be most important for the new employee in the first 1–3 months?
- How would you describe the ideal candidate for this position?
- What is most valuable to you in a candidate’s resume or experience?
- How open is the company to candidates without commercial experience but with strong projects?
- How important is experience in this specific domain?
- Which teams or functions interact most often with this role?
- Are there internal levels? How does this position fit into the leveling system?
- What salary range is предусмотрed for this position?
- Is there a bonus component, performance bonus, or annual bonus?
- How often is compensation reviewed?
- Is there a transparent compensation review system?
- Are compensation reviews tied to performance reviews?
- Are there stock options, shares, or long-term incentives?
- Are there restrictions on side jobs, open source, or pet projects?
- How does the company view public activity such as blogging, conferences, or meetups?
- Is there a budget for learning and professional development?
- How supportive is the company of internal transfers between teams?
- Are there career tracks for specialists and managers?
- If you look at people who are successful in the company, what do they have in common?
- If you look at people who had a hard time in the company, what was usually the reason?
- What advice would you give a candidate to prepare better for the next stages?
- Is there anything in my profile that you would recommend I explain in more detail in the next interviews?
- Are there any questions or doubts about my background that I can clarify already now?
- If I pass all stages successfully, what will the next step be and in what timeframe?
- What personally seems to you to be the strongest argument in favor of this company?
- What would you honestly call the most difficult aspect of this role or company?
- How does the company handle market changes, layoffs, or strategy shifts?
- Have there been any significant changes in the company or team recently?
- How often do priorities change at the business level?
- How stable is the product and direction for which you are hiring?
- Are there risks of team reorganization or structural changes?
- Who makes the final hiring decision?
- At which stages does the recruiter’s opinion have the greatest impact on the final decision?
- What personally makes a candidate memorable to you at the screening stage?

### 20.2 Questions for the Hiring Manager
- Can you describe what exactly the person in this role will be responsible for?
- How would you describe the main purpose of this position?
- Why is this position open right now?
- Is this a new role or a replacement?
- How does the role for which you are interviewing impact the team and the product?
- What tasks will come in the first weeks after joining?
- Which tasks do you consider the most important in the first 1–3 months?
- What are your expectations for a new person during the probation period?
- What would be considered a successful start in this role?
- What results would you like to see from the person after 3 months?
- What results would you like to see after 6–12 months?
- Which tasks in this role are regular, and which are project-based?
- How much time usually goes to features, bug fixing, support, technical debt, and research?
- What will be the hardest part of this role in the first months?
- What are the main problems or pain points you are trying to solve by hiring for this position?
- What is currently missing in the team that you hope the new person will bring?
- How is the team structured that you are hiring into?
- How many people are on the team?
- Which roles are represented on the team?
- Who will be the closest colleagues of the new hire?
- Who will the person in this role report to directly?
- How is collaboration organized with product, design, QA, analysts, and DevOps?
- How autonomous is this role in making decisions?
- Which decisions will the person be able to make independently?
- Which decisions need to be aligned with you or others?
- How do you usually delegate tasks and responsibility?
- What management style do you personally prefer?
- How do you conduct one-on-ones and how often?
- How do you give feedback?
- How do you understand that a person is on the right track?
- What does a “strong engineer” mean to you in your team?
- What does a “strong fullstack/backend/frontend engineer” mean specifically in the context of this role?
- Which skills are critical for success in this position?
- Which gaps in knowledge are acceptable if the candidate is strong in other areas?
- What is more important to you: depth in one area or breadth across the whole stack?
- How important is product involvement in this role?
- How important is communication with stakeholders in this role?
- How much ownership is expected from the person in this role?
- What balance between delivery and quality do you consider healthy?
- How are technical decisions made in the team?
- Who defines the architectural direction?
- How are disagreements about solution design or implementation resolved?
- How do you feel about bottom-up initiatives to improve processes, architecture, or quality?
- Can you give an example of a recent decision that had a strong impact on the team or product?
- What are the team’s main technical challenges right now?
- What are the team’s main product challenges right now?
- What are the most important projects or initiatives currently underway?
- How much of the work is related to new development, and how much to supporting legacy?
- How much legacy code is there in the area this role will own?
- How would you assess the current state of the codebase?
- Which codebase problems do you consider the most painful?
- Are there any major architectural or technology migrations currently underway?
- Are there any parts of the system that are especially fragile or complex?
- What in the current system would you most like to improve first?
- Which engineering practices in the team are already working well?
- Which engineering practices would you like to strengthen?
- How is code review organized?
- What are your expectations regarding code quality in the team?
- How is testing organized?
- What level of test coverage do you consider sufficient?
- Which types of tests are actually used in day-to-day work?
- How often do incidents happen because of insufficient tests or quality control?
- How are releases organized?
- How often does the team deploy changes?
- How safe and predictable is the release process?
- How does the team respond to urgent issues and incidents?
- Who participates in incident reviews?
- How do you run postmortems and follow-up after production issues?
- How is planning organized?
- What does the work cycle look like: sprints, kanban, quarterly planning?
- How often do priorities change?
- What usually causes priority changes?
- How do you balance business tasks and technical debt?
- How do you decide when to invest in refactoring or infrastructure?
- How do you estimate timelines and risks for tasks?
- How do you handle situations when timelines start to slip?
- What counts as a strong signal for you when evaluating a candidate?
- What counts as a red flag for you?
- What mistakes do candidates most often make in interviews for this role?
- Which questions, in your experience, help distinguish a strong candidate from an average one?
- Which qualities are especially important for this team beyond technical skills?
- How important is the ability to quickly understand someone else’s code in this role?
- How important are speed versus care, structure, and thoroughness?
- Does this role include on-call or incident response duties?
- Is there an expectation that the person will lead projects, not just implement tasks?
- Is there an expectation that the person will mentor others?
- Is there an expectation that the person will participate in hiring?
- Is there an expectation that the person will influence architecture or processes?
- How do you define boundaries of responsibility among engineers in the team?
- What differentiates someone who just “does tasks” from someone who really moves the team forward?
- How do you assess engineering maturity in employees?
- What counts as a good level of independence in your team?
- What do you expect from a person when requirements are incomplete or contradictory?
- How do you expect an engineer to act if they see a technical risk no one has considered?
- What do you expect from an engineer in a conflict between “ship fast” and “do it right”?
- How much space does the team have for experimentation and improvement?
- How do you feel about proposals to change approaches, libraries, or architecture?
- What trade-offs are most typical in your team right now?
- Where is the greatest uncertainty right now?
- What about this role is most likely to surprise someone after they join?
- What in this role usually turns out to be harder than it seems during interviews?
- What, on the contrary, usually turns out to be easier or more comfortable than candidates expect?
- What kinds of people usually thrive in your team?
- What kinds of people usually do not fit in, and why?
- How would you describe the team culture?
- How open is the team to discussing mistakes and feedback?
- How common is it in the team to ask for help?
- How much written communication and documentation is there?
- How distributed is the team, and how does that affect the processes?
- How would you assess the current maturity of the team’s processes?
- If you were joining this team again today, what would you want to know in advance?
- If I joined this role and turned out to be very successful in six months, what exactly would that mean?
- If you were choosing between two strong candidates, what could become the deciding factor?
- Which topics would you recommend studying especially deeply to succeed in this role?
- What growth opportunities does this position open up in one or two years?
- Which roles do people usually grow into from this position?
- Are there strong engineers in the team or company that one can learn from?
- Which initiatives or projects give the best chance to grow quickly?
- Are there examples of people who have grown within this team?
- By which criteria do people get promoted to the next level?
- How do you determine that someone is ready for the next level?
- Which skills separate junior from middle, middle from senior, and senior from lead in your system?
- How do you view a candidate who is not equally deep across the whole stack yet but learns quickly?
- Looking specifically at my profile, what strengths do you see?
- Looking specifically at my profile, what risks or gaps would you want to understand better?
- Is there anything in my background that you would like to hear more about in order to assess fit more accurately?
- What personally makes this team and role interesting to you?
- What do you like least about this role and team, honestly speaking?
- Why do you personally like working here?
- What would you change in the team if you had additional time and resources?
- If you had to choose between speed of hiring and quality of hiring, how do you usually balance that decision?
- What will the next step be after this interview, and how will you make the decision?

### 20.3 Questions for the Team
- How is the team currently structured, and which roles does it consist of?
- How many people are on the team, and how are responsibilities divided?
- Who interacts with whom on a daily basis?
- How is collaboration organized between developers, QA, analysts, designers, and product managers?
- How cross-functional is the team?
- How long has the team existed in its current composition?
- What has changed most significantly in the team over the last six months?
- What does a typical working week look like for the team?
- What is your work rhythm: sprints, kanban, or a mixed approach?
- How many parallel tasks does one developer usually handle?
- How is task planning organized?
- How often do priorities change during work?
- How does the team react to urgent tasks and sudden context switching?
- How are daily / stand-up / sync meetings organized?
- Which meetings does the team consider useful, and which feel more forced?
- How much time does the team spend in meetings in an average week?
- Are there practices in the team that you yourselves consider overloaded or inefficient?
- How would you assess the team’s overall level of autonomy?
- To what extent do developers participate in discussing solutions rather than just receiving tasks from above?
- How are decisions made within the team?
- How much does engineers’ opinion actually influence what ultimately gets done?
- How do you usually argue about decisions: openly, through discussion, through leads?
- What happens if there is strong disagreement within the team on some issue?
- How would you describe the team’s communication style?
- How comfortable is it in the team to ask “stupid” questions?
- How do people usually ask for help?
- How quickly can you get help if you are stuck?
- How do code reviews usually work in your team?
- How many reviewers are usually involved in one pull request?
- What does the team look at first in a code review?
- What counts as a good code review in your team?
- What most often causes review comments?
- Does the team practice pair programming or joint debugging?
- How does the team feel about refactoring?
- Is there room in normal work to allocate time for improving code and infrastructure?
- What counts as “good enough” quality for a release?
- How does the team feel about tests?
- Who is mainly responsible for quality: developers, QA, or both together?
- How is testing organized before a release?
- How much does the team trust automated tests and pipelines?
- Are there releases that the team is afraid of?
- How often does the team release changes?
- How routine are releases, or is it stressful every time?
- How do incidents typically happen on your team: are they rare or a regular part of life?
- How does the team behave during a production incident?
- Do you have a blameless postmortem culture?
- What usually causes the most pain for the team: the codebase, processes, dependent teams, deadlines?
- What is the team’s main source of frustration right now?
- On the other hand, what works especially well in the team?
- Why do people like working here specifically?
- What keeps strong engineers on your team?
- Why do you think people leave the team?
- Who would be successful on this team, and who would struggle?
- What qualities are especially valued in a new person joining your team?
- What most often distinguishes people who integrate into the team quickly?
- What mistakes should a newcomer avoid in their first few months?
- What does onboarding a new developer look like?
- On average, how long does it take before someone delivers their first useful task to production?
- When do you know that a person has successfully integrated into the team?
- Is there documentation that genuinely helps a new person?
- What usually turns out to be the most unexpected thing for newcomers?
- How dependent are you on individual strong people?
- Do you have bus factor problems?
- How evenly is knowledge about the system distributed?
- How does the team share knowledge?
- Do you do internal tech docs, demos, or knowledge-sharing sessions?
- How do you usually document decisions?
- How do you know that the team is moving in the right direction?
- What metrics or signals do you look at within the team?
- How does the team measure its effectiveness, if at all?
- How focused is the team on business outcomes rather than just closing tasks?
- Does the team feel a connection between its work and user outcomes?
- Does the team have influence over the roadmap?
- What is considered success on the team?
- What is considered failure on the team?
- How is collaboration with neighboring teams organized?
- Where do problems most often arise at the boundaries between teams?
- How easy is it to align with neighboring teams on priorities and dependencies?
- Are there regular conflicts between engineering and product / QA / support / analytics?
- How are such conflicts usually resolved?
- How is on-call support or business-request support organized?
- Do developers participate in support after release?
- How often are developers interrupted by ad-hoc requests?
- What is the balance between new features and supporting the existing system?
- How much time goes into legacy-related tasks?
- How understandable and predictable is the codebase to work with?
- Are there parts of the system that everyone is afraid to touch?
- How does the team live with technical debt?
- Does the team have time to improve internal tools?
- How do you feel about experimenting with new approaches and tools?
- How conservative is the team in technical decisions?
- How much bottom-up initiative is encouraged?
- If I come in with an idea to improve a process or system, how likely is it that it would actually be considered?
- Does the team feel ownership over the product and the system?
- What would the team like to improve in the next 3–6 months?
- If you could change one thing about how the team works right now, what would it be?
- How would you describe the feedback culture on the team?
- How openly do people give each other feedback?
- Are there toxic patterns the team is actively dealing with?
- How safe is it to admit a mistake on the team?
- How does the team treat people with different levels of experience?
- Is there a sense of mentorship and support for juniors / mid-level engineers?
- How does the team help people grow technically?
- How does the team help people grow in product and communication skills?
- What topics come up most often in retrospectives?
- Do retrospectives lead to real changes, or do they mostly stay at the level of discussion?
- What does a typically successful developer on your team look like after six months?
- What advice would you give to someone joining your team?
- What do you wish you had known about the team before joining?

### 20.4 Questions for the Tech Lead / Architect
- How would you describe the current system architecture as a whole?
- What are the main components or services in the system?
- Where are the key boundaries between modules or services?
- What architectural style is currently used, and why was it chosen?
- If you were designing the system from scratch today, what would you do differently?
- Which architectural decisions have been the most successful?
- Which architectural decisions currently cause the most pain?
- What are the most difficult technical trade-offs in the system?
- What is considered the most fragile part of the architecture right now?
- Are there parts of the system the team is afraid to change?
- What are the main constraints of the system that you take into account during development?
- What currently limits product development speed the most: architecture, processes, infrastructure, or people?
- How are responsibilities divided between teams at the architectural level?
- How clearly are ownership and service / module boundaries defined?
- Where do architectural conflicts between teams arise most often?
- How do you make architectural decisions?
- Who makes the final decision on technical matters?
- How centralized or distributed are architectural decisions across teams?
- Do you use ADRs, RFCs, or other decision-recording practices?
- How do you document architecture?
- Is architecture documentation alive and maintained, or more formal and static?
- How often is the architecture reviewed?
- Do you have regular architecture reviews?
- How do you know that an architectural decision turned out to be wrong?
- What signals tell you it is time to change the architecture?
- How do you approach evolving the system without doing a big rewrite from scratch?
- How common is it to make incremental changes instead of large rewrites?
- What major migrations or architectural changes have happened recently?
- What major migrations are planned in the near future?
- What architectural risks do you consider the most serious over the next year?
- How do you balance delivery speed and architectural sustainability?
- How do you decide when something is “good enough” versus when you need to invest in a stronger solution?
- How does the company decide to invest in technical debt reduction and platform improvements?
- How easy is it to justify architectural investments to the business?
- Do you have a technical strategy for the next 6–12 months?
- If so, what are its main directions?
- How is the technical strategy connected to business goals?
- How ready is the architecture for product growth right now?
